must_know.fact: Sequential programs run line by line, top to bottom, so the order of statements matters.
input() always returns a string, so the value must be cast before doing math.
Use int() for whole numbers (people, days, items) and float() for decimals (temperature, miles, gallons).
Naming convention: read input into a variable ending in Str (e.g., valueStr), then cast it into a variable without the Str suffix.
/ is division and always gives a decimal; // is floor division and drops the decimal; % (modulo) gives the remainder.
A comparison (==, !=, >, <, >=, <=) produces a Boolean value: True or False.
= assigns a value; == compares two values.
Fahrenheit to Celsius: C = (F - 32) * 5 / 9, with parentheses so 32 is subtracted first.
A Boolean expression can be stored in a variable and printed without an if statement (e.g., withinLimits = guests <= capacity).
% 7 wraps a day number around the week, always giving a value from 0 to 6.
Accumulator pattern: start total at 0, then total = total + num adds each new value to the running sum.
math.ceil() rounds up and math.floor() rounds down; import math goes at the top of the file.
\n prints a new line and \t prints a tab; escape characters start with a backslash.

traps.topic: ceil and floor of a negative number

traps.correct: round(3.4567) gives 4 (a whole number); round(3.4567, 2) gives 3.46
4000 seconds is 1 h 6 m 40 s (hours = totalSec // 3600, leftover = totalSec % 3600)
traps.common_mistake: uses / instead of //, or gets 1 h 7 m
